contracts.commit_point: run_command_sync(command, root) invoked at execute.py:50, whose subprocess.run(command, shell=True, cwd=str(root), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=...) at execute.py:15-22 spawns the shell process.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Pre-commit approval gate inside the run_command wrapper (execute.py:44-47): unless auto_approve is true, it calls request_approval(command) and, if the callback is absent or returns false, returns the refusal string "Command was not approved by the user and did not run: {command}" before run_command_sync is reached (fail-closed on a missing callback). The request_approval callback is supplied as backend main.py's on_command_approval (main.py:764-778), which pauses the run, broadcasts a 'command_approval' event, and blocks the worker thread on a threading.Event until POST /graphs/{graph_id}/run/{run_id}/command-approval (main.py:1033-1040) sets entry['approved'] (initialized False) and releases the event. Human approval is opt-out only via the explicit auto_approve_commands flag, default False in RunOptions (main.py:921-927), accepted by the run/redo/continue-from endpoints and threaded into run_graph (main.py:859) and into the tool build via get_crewai_tools' auto_approve_commands parameter (registry.py:73, 93).
contracts.forbidden_condition: run_command invoking run_command_sync (and thereby subprocess.run with shell=True) for a command when the run was not started with auto_approve_commands and no human approval for that exact command has been delivered through the command-approval bridge — including the case where no approval callback is present, in which the tool must refuse rather than execute.
pending_binding_information: toru_agents/crew_engine.py (the run_graph implementation) is not in the supplied views: the internal call site linking run_graph's on_command_approval / auto_approve_commands parameters to get_crewai_tools' request_command_approval / auto_approve_commands (and thus to build_run_command_tool) is not directly evidenced.

Whether the 'deterministic compile_check node' mentioned in run_command_sync's docstring (execute.py:12-13) exists in supplied flows and whether it executes commands without approval cannot be assessed from the provided source.

resolve_command_approval (main.py:1033-1040) resolves pending entries by run_id only and does not verify that the path's graph_id matches the pending run's graph; whether decisions are scoped to the intended graph is not established.

The identity/authentication of the human resolving an approval at /command-approval is not established in the supplied source; the obligation says 'a human approves' but no approver-binding fact is evidenced.
Whether shipped agent configurations actually include run_command in their tool lists (prevalence) is unknown; behavior labels are unavailable per the unit scope.
contracts.protected_operation: Invocation of the run_command agent tool by the agent to execute a shell command inside the workspace sandbox.
contracts.protected_resource: OS shell/process execution scoped to the agent's workspace sandbox root (subprocess.run(command, shell=True, cwd=str(root), ...) in run_command_sync).
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent-initiated shell commands submitted through the run_command tool must not be executed (run_command_sync / subprocess.run on the workspace sandbox root) until a human approves the exact command via the command-approval bridge, unless the run was explicitly started with auto_approve_commands.
scope_limits: Explicit bypass: a run started with auto_approve_commands=True skips the approval gate entirely (execute.py:44); the flag defaults to False (main.py:921-922) but is accepted by /graphs/{graph_id}/run, /redo, and /chats/{chat_id}/continue-from/{step_index} (main.py:937, 978, 1014).

The guard is enforced only in the run_command tool wrapper; run_command_sync is shared and itself unguarded (its docstring at execute.py:12-13 says it is 'Shared by the run_command tool and the deterministic compile_check node'), so any other caller of run_command_sync is outside this contract.

Fail-closed but availability-dependent: with request_approval=None and auto_approve false, the tool refuses to run (execute.py:45); the ability to obtain human approval (not merely refusal) depends on a callback actually being wired in.
Approval binds to the exact command string passed to request_approval; no canonicalization or normalization of the command occurs before the human decision.
Coverage is limited to the supplied source views; no claim is made about runtime behavior, safety outcome, or prevalence.
